renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Ah, honeyed past honey, the foretaste of waiting on the Gracious -- where, in what tick, turns it not ever-new? Ever unflagging, peopling the triple sphere with hundred fancies, yet single, seamless, triumphs the Birthless.

By lore-lamp licking the birth-greased wont-wick clean -- O God, when shall I stand in thy sight, prithee? For but a blink, with faults outworn, to lodge thy tread in heart -- then what, past thy doing? Blest I, quits I, big am I -- firm may that fancy stand, grounded his whom thou groundest, Lord.

All fair and foul thou makest thyself -- yet love of thee mothers the fair alone, solely, Lord. Mind glass-clear, Master -- steppest thou within, or at thy stepping clears it? Man dangles thus. Nay, here stands sure -- thy watch and only thine: mind's favour, Master, is fulfilment, the remotest seat. Word, wit, work, this frame of mine, Lord, grace them to gleam love-trimmed for thee sole. This praise-gem, heavy with granted longings, luck's lodging of love -- for the Gracious wrought teacher Bhatta Narayana.

paragraphs.text: Ah, honeyed past honey, the pre-taste of waiting on the Gracious -- what tick does it not go ever-new? Ever unflagging, filling triple spheres with hundred daydreams, yet single, no-seam, the Birthless takes it.

By lore-lamp licking the birth-greased wont-wick clean -- O God, when do I pull up in thy sight, prithee? One blink, faults outworn, thy step lodged in chest -- then what, past thy doing? Blest me, quits me, big me -- may that vaunt stand, grounded whose grounder is thee, Lord.

Fair and foul alike thou makest thyself -- yet love of thee mothers only fair, solely, Lord. Mind glass-clear, Master -- steppest thou within, or at thy stepping clears it? Man dangles, truly. Nay, locked here -- thy watch and only thine: mind's favour, Master, is the prize, the farthest seat. Word, wit, work, this frame of mine, Lord, grace it to gleam love-trimmed for thee only. This praise-gem, heavy with granted longings, luck's home of love -- for the Gracious built teacher Bhatta Narayana.
